# Draft API consumers and compatibility classes

Captured from the draft repository `github.com/shakhbanov/whisperer` at commit `589917e84` on 2026-10-01. The route table and OpenAPI come from the draft application assembled in a throwaway environment with local placeholder settings (`contracts/tools/generate_draft_baseline.py`). Consumers were found by reading each client's source. File references point into the draft repository.

| Class | Meaning | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `native` | Used by live code of a working native client (macOS 1.4.5, Windows 1.4.5), including the WhispererKit modules macOS uses | Must stay compatible: shipped clients are not updated (nfr-12) |
| `external` | Used by an external party: acquirer, LiveKit and calendar webhooks, MCP and OAuth clients, links in emails and shared links, search engines | Must stay compatible |
| `web` | Used only by the draft web frontend | May change together with the v2 frontend |
| `unused` | No live consumer found | Not carried over unless D4 keeps it |
| `excluded` | Not part of the contract: the draft's own probes and monitoring | Not checked |

### whispererkit — WhispererKit, the shared Swift networking package

Base URL `https://whisperer.one/v1` from `Info.plist`; paths are appended without a trailing slash. TLS public keys are pinned (`Config.swift:174-177`): the production certificate must keep one of the two pinned SPKI hashes (Let's Encrypt YE1 or ISRG Root YE). The Linux transport follows no redirects, keeps no cookies and sends `Accept-Encoding: identity`, so a redirect or a compressed body on any API endpoint breaks it. Dates must be ISO-8601 with a time zone; meeting note and import responses use camelCase keys (`draftMarkdown`, `jobId`, `fileName`, `meetingId`). UUIDs in paths and in `sid`/`hub_id` are upper case. `POST me/storage/knowledge`, `PUT me/models/roles/{role}` and `POST knowledge/sources/{id}/sync` must answer with a JSON body, not 204. On `/v1/ws/realtime` a 401 or 403 handshake stops reconnecting. `/v1/ws/user` `hello` always sends `client: "desktop_macos"`. `GET /v1/scripts` must keep answering 404 (feature hidden). Calls made from the kit modules Hub, Knowledge, Leo, Proactive, Rooms, Search and Workspace are recorded but do not make an endpoint must-keep: the macOS app references no type declared in those modules, so only the unshipped iOS app reaches them.

### macos — macOS app

Almost all networking goes through WhispererKit; the app sets only `Authorization` and `Content-Type` itself. `openAdminPage("/cabinet/leo?reminder=<id>")` sends `?` as `%3F` and works only because the top-level fallback decodes the path and redirects to `/app/cabinet/leo?reminder=…` (`web_static.py:764-773`).

No backend URL of its own: everything goes through WhispererKit. Release builds use `https://whisperer.one/v1` with certificate pinning. REST calls use HTTP/1.1 with `Connection: close` and `Accept-Encoding: identity`; no cookie store, no User-Agent, no redirects.

### windows — Windows app

Pins Let's Encrypt YE1 or ISRG Root YE for `whisperer.one` and `www.whisperer.one` (`Network/CertificatePinner.cs:41-56`). Sends `X-Client-Kind: desktop` on login with `captcha_token: null`, so desktop logins must stay exempt from the captcha. Reads errors from `{"detail": "..."}` (auth) and `{"detail": {"code": ...}}` (voice translation, audio upload). Saves meeting notes to `/v1/sessions/{id}/note[/draft]`, which does not exist in the draft (see unmatched calls). Never sends User-Agent, version, device id or locale headers.

### web — Web frontend (the cabinet SPA)

axios with base URL `/v1` and credentials; `Authorization: Bearer` from memory; `X-CSRF-Token` from the `meetassist_csrf` cookie on `/auth/*`; one refresh-and-retry on 401. Room-token clients for `/v1/meeting-ai`, `/v1/subtitles`, `/v1/whiteboard`, `/v1/streams/live`. Opens absolute paths outside `/app` (`/studio/{id}`, `/rooms/{id}`, `/meetings/{id}`, `/cabinet?paid=1`) that rely on the top-level fallback redirect.

## Must-keep operations with untyped draft responses

The draft declares no response schema for these, so the harness cannot compare their shape. The owning slice verifies them against recorded responses (D2 fixtures) and the fields the clients read.
